transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I’m having a hard time staying focused on a task long enough to finish it, even when it’s important. At work, I’ll start tracing a client’s network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I’ve read the same log entries three times and still don’t know what they say.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focus?
About a year and ten months now. It really got serious after I was fired—I lost the systems that had been keeping me on track.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or focus when you were growing up in school?
Yeah. My mom still jokes that my grade-school report cards always said I was bright, but I couldn’t stay in my seat, I’d blurt out answers, and I’d lose homework even when I’d actually done it.
Do you currently find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still?
Yeah. If I’m sitting with a client or at a chess meeting, my leg is usually bouncing. I’ll click a pen or keep turning a cable tie in my fingers until somebody gives me that look.
